scope: Production-required distributed API request limiting, explicit reverse-proxy trust, privacy-safe network keys, fail-closed dependency behavior, and reference edge routing

priorDefect.control: one in-process IP budget per API replica
priorDefect.failureMode: Horizontal scaling multiplied the effective request budget, and no repository-owned edge policy or explicit trusted-proxy contract proved the pre-authentication client identity.

implementedControls: production startup rejects an empty trusted direct-proxy CIDR allowlist
proxy configuration rejects malformed, duplicate, whitespace-ambiguous, more-than-16-entry, and IPv4/IPv6 /0 trust
Redis limiting requires a stable 32-to-64-random-byte base64url key shared by all environment replicas
a dedicated Redis client uses bounded connect and command timeouts, one request retry, no offline queue, and startup ping
all replicas share a fixed 120-request-per-60-second budget while existing sensitive route limits remain
the limiter key is an environment namespace plus HMAC-SHA-256 of Fastify's proxy-verified client address
limiter keys contain no raw address, authorization value, organization ID, tenant data, or financial data
Redis store errors prevent route-handler execution rather than silently failing open
an exceeded budget returns 429 RATE_LIMITED with an application-generated correlation ID
process liveness bypasses the application limiter to prevent Redis-driven restart storms
the Nginx reference applies an outer connected-peer budget to browser /api/ and direct /v1/ traffic
browser API and authentication traffic remains on the Next.js BFF while versioned direct API traffic preserves its path to Fastify
the corrected public Nginx edge overwrites X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-IP with its observed connected peer; the original append strategy was unsafe and is superseded by live edge evidence
operations documentation forbids production fail-open/local recovery, global proxy trust, and mixed-key rolling rotation

checks: exact dependency-policy validation across 20 package manifests
production builds across all applicable workspace projects, including Next.js

covered: one exact shared 120-request budget across two independent Fastify instances
request 121 returns 429 and does not invoke the route
rate-limit response includes stable code, safe message, and generated correlation ID
shared-store error fails closed without route execution
raw client address is absent from Redis keys
an untrusted connected peer cannot select its identity with X-Forwarded-For
a trusted direct proxy resolves the first untrusted hop and ignores attacker-controlled prefixes
125 liveness requests do not consume the normal API budget
invalid environment namespace and HMAC key material fail before route registration
production rejects local store, missing key, empty/global/malformed/duplicate proxy trust, and invalid timeouts
connected-peer X-Real-IP and X-Forwarded-For authority checks, corrected to require overwrite after the original validator incorrectly accepted append behavior
client body-size and slow-body timeout ceilings
rejection of direct client-supplied X-Forwarded-For forwarding
edgeStaticCoverage.runtimeInterpretation: Historical result only: the validator incorrectly accepted $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for at the public edge. That preserved an attacker-selected prefix and could influence Fastify's proxy-resolved limiter address. The validator and configuration now require $remote_addr overwrite; the superseding live edge artifact records parser and observed-response behavior.

browserRegression.interpretation: No web application source changed in this increment. The reference Nginx routing is not exercised by the local browser harness and remains runtime evidence.

missingConfiguration: DATABASE_ADMIN_URL and related PostgreSQL role URLs
plannedRateLimitCoverage: two separate Redis clients and two independent Fastify instances share one random test namespace
121 concurrent requests produce exactly 120 successful responses and one 429
only one pseudonymous namespaced key exists and it contains no raw address
the shared key has a positive bounded expiry
liveIntegrationAttempt.interpretation: No live integration assertion ran. The new Redis case is a defined test, not passing runtime evidence.

operationalImpact.storeFailurePolicy: fail request admission closed while process liveness remains available
operationalImpact.keyRotationEffect: resets pseudonymous counters; mixed old/new replica keys temporarily create parallel budgets
operationalImpact.rollback: Keep the reviewed edge budget and equivalent distributed enforcement, or temporarily constrain the API to one replica. Do not restore an unverified process-local multi-replica production budget.

remainingEvidenceAndOperationalRisks: This list records the boundary at generation time; artifacts/live-edge-verification-2026-07-29.json supersedes the Nginx authority/runtime items.
Run the two-client Redis integration test against the supported production Redis version and configuration.
Parse and execute the reference or equivalent Nginx configuration in a production-like network.
Prove the exact direct-proxy CIDRs and spoofed forwarding-header behavior through every ingress/load-balancer hop.
Measure edge and application limits under representative burst, sustained, multi-address, webhook, auth, and expensive-route load.
Exercise Redis startup failure, runtime failure, recovery, readiness behavior, and alert delivery without enabling fail-open behavior.
Exercise coordinated HMAC-key rotation and prove that no mixed-key replica window remains.
Confirm acceptable NAT/shared-egress false-positive behavior and document any reviewed endpoint/user budget extension.

This artifact makes no production, staging, multi-host, Nginx runtime, live Redis, load, recovery, rotation, or alert claim; later local live Redis, readiness, and edge evidence is recorded separately.
